overview: Kinsale grew Q2 2026 diluted operating EPS 15.9% to $5.54 with a 75.5% combined ratio and 24.4% annualized operating ROE, even as gross written premium fell 5% on shrinkage in the Commercial Property Division. Excluding that division GWP rose 3.7%, and the company added a $250M buyback authorization while its pricing trend fell 5.9%.
keyTakeaways: Michael Kehoe, Chairman, President and CEO, called commercial property "definitely a buyer's market" and said Kinsale is writing a shrinking volume there.
Stuart Winston, Chief Underwriting Officer, said London competition is spreading into long-tail casualty lines and depressing Construction pricing.
Kehoe raised buyback capacity to $337M and called it the principal capital allocation strategy while growth is limited.
Salmaan Allibhai, Chief Analytics and Technology Officer, put casualty loss cost trend at probably mid-single digits with little social inflation.
financialHighlights: Diluted operating EPS was $5.54, up 15.9% from $4.78, with net income up 31.1% and net operating earnings up 13.3%.
Gross written premium fell 5% and net written premium 1.4%, while net earned premium rose 8.9%.
The 75.5% combined ratio included 4.5 points of favorable prior-year development and 1.3 points of cat losses.
The expense ratio rose to 21.7% from 20.7% on a higher net commission ratio from larger reinsurance retentions.
guidance: Bryan Petrucelli, CFO, said the Q2 expense ratio of 21.7% is a good measure going forward, with a possible slight commission uptick after the June 1 reinsurance renewal.
Michael Kehoe, Chairman, President and CEO, said Commercial Property comparisons ease modestly in H2 because 60% of the division's premium was written in last year's first half.
Stuart Winston, Chief Underwriting Officer, said nine new products launched this year, five more launch imminently and 10 are in the pipeline.
Petrucelli cited new money yields around 5.25% and average duration of four and a quarter years.

qa.question: When will property pricing reach equilibrium, should the accident year loss ratio drift up with mix, and how will buybacks be paced?
qa.answer: Kehoe had no insight on timing and said Kinsale will keep leaning into buybacks with about $80M left on the prior $250M plus a new $250M; Salmaan Allibhai, Chief Analytics and Technology Officer, said the loss ratio could drift up over time.
qa.read: Answered partially; no timing or loss ratio figure.

qa.question: Is inbound account growth from broker engagement or pricing, and what are casualty loss trends?
qa.answer: Winston said both, with an idle broker initiative re-engaging lapsed brokers and steady hit ratios; Salmaan Allibhai, Chief Analytics and Technology Officer, put casualty loss trend at mid-single digits, and Michael Kehoe said IBNR release is being slowed in longer-tail lines.

qa.question: What drove the better current accident year loss ratio, and will the ceding commission keep rising?
qa.answer: Allibhai cited normal variability with losses below expectations and reserves as conservative as ever; Bryan Petrucelli, CFO, said only one month of the June 1 treaty is in Q2, so a slight commission uptick may be offset by AI efficiency.
qa.read: Answered partially; no loss ratio driver isolated.

qa.question: How much are casualty ROEs compressing as E&S softens?
qa.answer: Kehoe said everything is managed to a 20% ROE or greater, most lines run ahead of it, and quarterly ROE was 24.4%.
qa.read: Answered partially; broker commission question not addressed.

unanswered.question: Whether Kinsale will change broker commissions in a softer market.
unanswered.how: Michael Kehoe, Chairman, President and CEO, discussed service and risk appetite without indicating any change.

unanswered.question: Whether Q2 is the trough for commercial property pricing.
unanswered.how: Stuart Winston, Chief Underwriting Officer, said there is "no telling where it's going to go in 2027."

unanswered.question: The growth uplift from new products.
unanswered.how: Winston described a "crawl, walk, run" rollout with no quantification.
